# Bubble

A chat message in a bubble that shows who sent it.

:label[Left out of Content first]{tone="warning"} Readers need sections, navigation and little else. Bubbles are for back-and-forth chat, and the catalogue rules them out for long text. Use instead: [Card](./card)

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** A back-and-forth conversation between people or with an assistant.
- **Not when:** Comments on a page or long text (use a message or a card).

Instead:

- [Message](./message.md): One message with its author and time, without the bubble shape.

<a class="odv-anatref" href="./bubble/anatomy"><span class="odv-anatref-b"><b>Anatomy reference</b><span>Every part of the bubble, the job it does, and the decisions behind it. 4 parts.</span></span><span class="odv-anatref-go" aria-hidden="true">→</span></a>

## Words

- Write to one person: "you", not "users".
- Short sentences with room to breathe.
- Explain why before asking for anything.
- Use: Read, Save for later, You, Next issue. Avoid: Click here, Submit, Users, Content.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Not now
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Browse guides

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add bubble
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Bubble reads 11 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Bubble's tokens to change Bubble alone.
